question.prompt:
In the figure, \(\angle A,\) \(\angle B\) and \(\angle C\) are right angles. If \(\angle AEB = 40^\circ\) and \(\angle BED = \angle BDE,\) then \(\angle CDE =\)

[Figure 1](figures/1995_AMC_8_Q13_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Start with triangle \(BED\): its right angle and its two equal angles determine the angle next to the given \(40^\circ\) angle.

[Figure 1](figures/1995_AMC_8_Q13_question_fig1.svg)

Since the angles of a triangle total \(180^\circ\),
\[
\angle BED=\angle BDE
=\frac{180^\circ-90^\circ}{2}=45^\circ.
\]
Ray \(EB\) lies inside \(\angle AED\), so
\[
\angle AED=40^\circ+45^\circ=85^\circ.
\]
Now consider the outer quadrilateral \(ACDE\). A quadrilateral's interior angles total \(360^\circ\), because a diagonal splits it into two triangles. Its angles at \(A\) and \(C\) are both \(90^\circ\), giving
\[
\angle CDE
=360^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ-85^\circ
=95^\circ.
\]
Therefore the answer is \(\boxed{95^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Use the outer quadrilateral

solutions.explanation:
The right angles at \(A\) and \(C\) show that \(AE\) and \(CD\) are both perpendicular to \(AC\). Hence \(AE\parallel CD\), which lets us relate the angles at the ends of transversal \(ED\).

First find \(\angle BED\). Triangle \(BED\) has \(\angle EBD=90^\circ\) and \(\angle BED=\angle BDE\), so its two remaining angles are each
\[
\frac{180^\circ-90^\circ}{2}=45^\circ.
\]
Since ray \(EB\) lies inside \(\angle AED\),
\[
\angle AED=\angle AEB+\angle BED
=40^\circ+45^\circ=85^\circ.
\]
The interior angles \(\angle AED\) and \(\angle CDE\) lie on the same side of transversal \(ED\) between the parallel lines, so they sum to \(180^\circ\). Therefore
\[
\angle CDE=180^\circ-85^\circ=95^\circ.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{95^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Use the parallel sides
